iWant: when Squire cannot fix something, to see exactly what a support ticket will say and send it only if I say yes
soThat: I get help without giving away anything personal
description: The ticket journey: a failed self-fix, a ticket of allow-listed diagnostics, an exact preview including the install's identity details, a yes or a no, the intake on the product site, the private tracker and daily triage. A ticket the intake cannot take yet is saved on the Mac and sent later. The receiving end is built in the site's repository; until it exists, the ticket criteria are proven against a local stand-in intake.
title: Support tickets: previewed, sent on a yes, diagnostics only, anonymous

acceptanceCriteria.description: A support ticket is sent only on the Squire owner's yes, after a preview showing exactly what will be sent.
acceptanceCriteria.given: A ticket Squire has built and previewed, including the install's identity details
acceptanceCriteria.when: The Squire owner says yes, or says no or does not answer
acceptanceCriteria.then: On a yes, the bytes posted equal the bytes previewed, identity details included; on a no or no answer, nothing is posted.

acceptanceCriteria.description: A support ticket holds diagnostics about Squire and the Mac only, never the Squire owner's personal details.
acceptanceCriteria.given: Personal details planted in the Squire owner's folder, in error messages and in paths (names, email addresses, phone and card numbers)
acceptanceCriteria.when: Squire builds a ticket and it is sent
acceptanceCriteria.then: The ticket carries only allow-listed diagnostic fields, and none of the planted details appears in it or anywhere it is sent.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Tickets never make the Squire owner identifiable, the receiver keeps nothing beyond codes, and a ticket's data is deleted at the Squire owner's request.
acceptanceCriteria.when: The receiver files them, and the Squire owner later asks for a ticket to be deleted
acceptanceCriteria.then: The install id is random and linked to no person; the receiver stores codes only; after the deletion request the ticket's data is gone end to end.

acceptanceCriteria.description: A ticket the Squire owner said yes to is kept and retried exactly as approved when sending it fails.
acceptanceCriteria.given: A ticket the Squire owner has said yes to
acceptanceCriteria.when: Sending it fails, Squire is offline, or whether it arrived is unclear
acceptanceCriteria.then: The exact approved ticket is saved and shown as waiting to send; Squire retries it without sending it twice when it can, and never changes it without another yes.

acceptanceCriteria.description: A ticket field whose value is outside its closed set or pattern, or that the privacy patterns match, is left out of the ticket.
acceptanceCriteria.given: Diagnostics with a value outside its field's closed set or fixed pattern (a Mac model, a macOS version or a Claude Code version answer carrying words, names or addresses), or a value inside its pattern that the privacy patterns match (a card or phone number, an email address, the account's names)
acceptanceCriteria.then: That field is dropped, the rest of the ticket is built from the allow-listed fields, and the value appears neither in the preview nor in anything sent.

acceptanceCriteria.description: An approved ticket whose send fails in any way is kept and retried exactly as approved, never sent changed.
acceptanceCriteria.given: A ticket the Squire owner said yes to, whose send fails, finds the intake offline, gets its answer only after the time allowed, or whose waiting file has changed since the yes
acceptanceCriteria.then: The ticket stays waiting with a health line saying so, and is retried carrying the same bytes and ticket id until an answer in the 2xx range clears it, filed once; a changed ticket is never sent until the Squire owner says yes again to the changed text.
